questions.question: In organic chemistry, which of the following is an empirical rule used to predict the regioselectivity of electrophilic addition reactions of alkanes and alkynes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Markovnikov's rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Markovnikov's rule:
 
 
• Markovnikov's rule is a principle that predicts the outcome of an addition reaction of an unsymmetrical alkene.
 
• It states that in the addition of a polar reagent to an unsymmetrical alkene, the electrophile will add to the carbon atom that has the most hydrogen atoms attached to it, while the nucleophile will add to the carbon atom that has the least hydrogen atoms attached to it.
 
• This is because the more substituted carbocation intermediate is more stable due to the electron-donating effect of the alkyl groups.
 
• This rule is named after Russian chemist Vladimir Markovnikov who first proposed it in 1869.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Rule
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Cornforth's rules
 
 
A set of rules that predict the stereochemistry of certain types of organic reactions.

 
Rule 1: In an electrocyclic reaction, the new sigma bond is formed in such a way as to maximize the overlap of the interacting orbitals.

 
Rule 2: In a cycloaddition reaction, the new sigma bonds are formed in such a way as to minimize the number of four-membered rings formed.

 
 
 

 Bredt's rule
 
 
A rule that states that a double bond cannot be located at the bridgehead of a bridged bicyclic system if it leads to a strained conformation.

 
This is because the double bond would introduce additional ring strain, making the molecule less stable.

 
 
 

 Baldwin's rules
 
 
A set of rules that describe the feasibility and stereochemistry of intramolecular reactions.

 
The rules specify the minimum number of atoms in the transition state of a reaction, as well as the angles between the reacting bonds.

 
The rules are as follows:

 
Rule 1: The number of atoms in the transition state of a reaction cannot exceed the number of atoms in the smallest ring that can be drawn around the reacting bonds.

 
Rule 2: The angles between the reacting bonds must correspond to bond angles in stable molecules.

 
Rule 3: The reaction must proceed through a transition state that is no more strained than the reactant or product.

questions.question: Particles of matter are continuously moving due to their:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy that an object possesses due to its motion.
 
• All particles of matter are in constant motion, and this motion is a result of their kinetic energy.
 
• The temperature of a substance is a measure of the average kinetic energy of its particles.
 
• Increased kinetic energy results in faster movement of particles, which can lead to changes in the state of matter (e.g., from solid to liquid).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy:**

 
 
• Kinetic energy is a form of energy that an object or a particle has by reason of its motion.
 
• It is defined as the work needed to accelerate a body of a given mass from rest to its stated velocity.
 
• Once the object reaches this velocity, it maintains its kinetic energy unless its speed changes.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy (KE) is given by KE = 1/2 mv², where m is the mass and v is the velocity.
 
 
 
• **Other Forms of Energy:**
 
 
• **Nuclear Energy:** Energy released during nuclear fission or fusion, especially when used to generate electricity.
 
• **Chemical Energy:** Energy stored in the bonds of chemical compounds, released in a chemical reaction.
 
• **Mechanical Energy:** The sum of kinetic and potential energy in an object that is used to do work.
 
 
 
• **State of Matter:**
 
 
• Solid: Particles are closely packed and only vibrate in place.
 
• Liquid: Particles are close together but can move/slide past one another.
 
• Gas: Particles are far apart and move freely.

questions.question: Ten years ago, the average age of A, B and C is 20 years. After ten years from now, the average age of A and B is 45 years. Find the present age of C.
questions.solution:
Given:

Ten years ago, the average age of A, B and C is 20 years. 

After ten years from now, the average age of A and B is 45 years.

Concept used:

The average age of A, B and C ('n' years ago) = a years

The average age of A, B and C (at present) = (a + n) years

The average age of A and B (after 'm' years) = b years

The average age of A and B (at present) = (b - m) years

Calculation:

The average age of A, B and C (ten years ago) = 20 years

The average age of A, B and C (at present) = 20 + 10 = 30 years

The sum of age of A, B and C (at present) = 30 × 3 = 90 years

The average age of A and B (after ten years) = 45 years

The average age of A and B (at present) = 45 - 10 = 35 years

The sum of age of A and B (at present) = 35 × 2 = 70 years

The present age of C = 90 - 70 = 20 years

∴ The present age of C is 20 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** Total age of A, B and C 10 years ago = 3 × 20 = 60 years

Total present age = 60 + (10 + 10 + 10) = 60 + 30 = 90

Total present age 10 year after = 90 + 30 = 120

Total age of A and B 10 years later = 45 × 2 = 90

So Age of C 10 years later = 120 - 90 = 30

Hence, Present age of C = 30 years - 10 years = 20 years

questions.question:
If an object is lying at rest on a surface, which of the following can you conclude about the force(s) acting on it?

(A): No force is acting on it.

(B): A pair of balanced forces is acting on it.

(C): Multiple pairs of balanced forces are acting on it.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**(B) or (C)**__

__**Concept:**__

Force: 

__
 
• It is an influence that tends to set a stationary body in motion or stop a moving body, or that tends to change the speed and direction of a moving body, or that tends to change the shape (and size) of a body.

Balanced forces:

 
• The resultant of all the forces acting on a body is called the balanced force.

 
 
• A body under the action of balanced forces does not change its position of rest( or of uniform motion) and it appears as if no force is acting on it.
 
• If several balanced forces act on a stationary body, the body continues to remain in its stationary position.
 
• If several balanced forces act on a body in uniform motion, the body continues to be in its state of uniform motion.
 
• Balanced forces cannot produce motion in a stationary body or stop a moving body; they can change the shape of a body.
 
 
• An example of a balanced force is the squeezing of a rubber ball or a balloon.
 
• In this case, we apply equal and opposite force on our hands.
 
 
 
 
 
• When the resultant of all the forces is not equal to zero, then it is called unbalanced forces

**Explanation:**__

 
• **No force is acting on it: **This statement is incorrect because even when an object is at rest, forces do act upon it. The absence of observable motion does not mean an absence of forces.
 
• Forces are in place to ensure the object stays at rest, but they are balanced, meaning their net sum is zero, ensuring the object does not move.
 
• **A pair of balanced forces are acting on it: **This **statement is correct.** The pair of forces here is the downward force of gravity and the normal (upward) force of the reaction from the surface.
 
• When an object lies at rest on a surface, the force of gravity pulling the object down is equal to the normal force pushing up from the surface, thereby remaining balanced and ensuring the object's state of equilibrium.
 
• **Multiple pairs of balanced forces acting on it:** could also be correct, depending on the circumstances. For instance, besides the downward force of gravity and the upward normal force, there can be other pairs of forces at play, such as static friction and an applied force.
 
• If you try to push the object, but it doesn't move, it means the static frictional force is equal and opposite to the applied push. Thus, there are multiple pairs of balanced forces keeping the object at rest.

**Based on the principles outlined by Newton's third law of motion and the concepts of balanced forces (B) and (C) are answers.**

questions.question: If X is 90 % of Y, what percentage of X is Y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume Y = 100.

Since X is 90% of Y, then X = 90.

Percentage of X that is Y = (Y ÷ X) × 100

Required % = (100 ÷ 90) × 100 = 1000 ÷ 9 = 111.11...

**∴ The correct answer is 111.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

X = 90% of Y

**Formula Used:**

Percentage = (Value ÷ Base) × 100

 
 Y (Total Base) = 100 units
 
 X (90% of Y) = 90 units
 
• 
 To find: (Y / X) × 100 = (100 / 90) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ X = (90 ÷ 100) × Y

⇒ X = 0.9 × Y

⇒ Y = X ÷ 0.9

⇒ Y = (10 ÷ 9) × X

⇒ Percentage of X that is Y = (Y ÷ X) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = [(10/9)X ÷ X] × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (10 ÷ 9) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 1000 ÷ 9

⇒ Required Percentage ≈ 111.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 111.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Change

If A is x% less than B, then B is [x ÷ (100 − x)] × 100% more than A.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert any fraction a/b to a percentage, multiply it by 100. Common conversion: 1/9 ≈ 11.11%.

Basic Percentage Formula

Percentage = (Part ÷ Whole) × 100. The "Whole" is always the value following the word "of" or "than".</p

**Conditions to follow:**__

• If there is any bracket, open the bracket, then add or subtract the terms. a + (b + c) = a + b + c, a + (b - c) = a + b - c
 
• If there is a negative sign just open the bracket, multiply the negative sign with each term inside the bracket. a – (b + c) ⇒ a – b – c 
 
• If there is any term just outside the bracket, multiply that outside term with each term inside the bracket. a(b + c) ⇒ ab + ac 

**Remember BODMAS Rule:**__

One easy way to remember the BODMAS rule is to perform these steps:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/415df2b0a808d428a4a482aa6e439d65e029a1aede312ba561c35170b6744535.png]
